title: A two-diode voltage reference
story: Two silicon diodes in series make a cheap reference voltage of about 1.3 V that barely moves when the supply changes. A 9 V supply feeds them through a resistor. Pick the resistor that puts them firmly into conduction without wasting current.
hints: Each diode drops roughly 0.65-0.7 V, so the pair drops about 1.35 V.
The resistor sees the rest of the 9 V: I = (9 - 1.35) / R.
Ten times the current raises each diode's voltage by only about 60 mV.
